claims.text: EVERY PROBE IS (prompt, checker) AND THE CHECKER IS DETERMINISTIC PYTHON. No model judges another model's answer.
claims.why: The chunk defines constants and nonce but does not contain any probe or checker implementations. The claim cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: unavailable (not signed in, bench asleep, CLI not installed) is NOT a failure and never trips the exit code; CANARY_STATUSES is closed and CanaryRun.summary reports the two groups separately, by construction.
claims.why: CANARY_STATUSES is defined as a closed tuple with 'unavailable' as a distinct status. FAILING_STATUSES explicitly excludes 'unavailable'. The claim about CanaryRun.summary is uncheckable but the status separation is confirmed.

claims.text: arrival and instruction ask 'did our bytes arrive intact and did the lane answer in the shape it was told to' -- that is LIVENESS, and a regression there is an alarm. anchoring and comprehension ask 'is this lane's reasoning the right shape for a job' -- that is QUALITY. A lane can be alive and still be the wrong shape for a job, so a quality regression is reported loudly and does NOT trip the exit code.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the definitions of build_arrival, check_arrival, etc. The separation of liveness vs quality is stated but not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: every host is passed EXPLICITLY per call; this module never sets, mutates or exports OLLAMA_HOST into any process environment (the subprocess environment is vendors.council_env, which strips it);
claims.why: This chunk does not contain any code that sets environment variables or calls subprocesses. The claim cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: only 127.0.0.1/localhost counts as local. The bench is another box on the tailnet and a canary payload sent there HAS left this machine, which is why every probe body is synthetic -- generated filler, fruit names and invented one-line summaries. A canary is not a place to ship repo source off the machine, and there is no code path here that reads a repo file.
claims.why: The chunk defines _FILLER_WORDS, _TAIL_WORDS, _ANCHOR_SETS which are synthetic and not repo source. The comment on _FILLER_WORDS explicitly says 'SYNTHETIC ONLY, never repo source'. No file reading code is present in this chunk.

claims.text: run_canary takes live and it DEFAULTS TO FALSE. Any lane still carrying a shipped vendor transport raises LiveCanaryRefused before a thread is started, before a probe is built and before one byte is dispatched.
claims.why: The function run_canary is not defined in this chunk. The claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: The classification is session.live_egress_seats -- IMPORTED, not re-implemented.
claims.why: Line imports live_egress_seats from .session, confirming it is imported and not re-implemented.

claims.text: live_egress_lanes only maps a Lane back to the adapter(s) behind its ask callable and hands them to that one function.
claims.why: The function live_egress_lanes is not defined in this chunk. The claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: CANARY_STATUSES: CLOSED -- nothing may invent a sixth, and in particular unavailable and wrong_answer are separate members because a report that merges them is a report that lies.
claims.why: CANARY_STATUSES is defined as a tuple with exactly five strings: ok, wrong_answer, timeout, unavailable, error. No sixth status is present.

claims.text: Only liveness trips the exit code -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: The exit code logic is not in this chunk. The claim about liveness tripping exit code cannot be verified.

claims.text: unavailable is deliberately absent: we never asked, so there is nothing to have failed.
claims.why: FAILING_STATUSES is defined as frozenset({'wrong_answer', 'timeout', 'error'}) which does not include 'unavailable'.

claims.text: Fresh PER PROBE PER LANE, not per run: a reused nonce cannot distinguish a lane that answered from a lane (or a cache, or a shared transcript) that echoed somebody else's answer -- which is the exact confusion the anchoring incident was made of.
claims.why: The function new_nonce generates a random nonce each call, but the claim about per-probe-per-lane usage is about how it is called, not how it is defined. The calling pattern is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The prompt varies every run (a probe a model has memorised measures nothing) while the checker still knows the right answer without carrying state between the two halves of a probe.
claims.why: _rng seeds a random.Random with the nonce string, ensuring deterministic but varying randomness per nonce without shared state.

claims.text: Disjoint from _FILLER_WORDS on purpose: the arrival tail token must not be findable anywhere in the padding, or a reply could satisfy the tail check by quoting the middle of the prompt.
claims.why: The sets _FILLER_WORDS and _TAIL_WORDS are defined with no overlapping words (verified by inspection: e.g., 'lantern' vs 'harbor', etc.).

observations.what: The comment on _FILLER_WORDS states 'None of these describes a real file in this repo, and none of them may contain roll/revert', but the chunk ends before the comment is complete. The claim about 'roll/revert' is uncheckable.
